title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. S = k{T} is the divided-power polynomial algebra in one variable, with T^{(ℓ)}T^{(k)} = C(k+ℓ,ℓ) T^{(k+ℓ)}. The surrounding theorem says that for a k-module M and N ≥ 0, the graded module M⊗S is recovered from its truncation τ_N(M⊗S). Equivalently, for 0 ≤ i < N there is an isomorphism M ≅ (M⊗S)_i ≅ Hom^i(τ_{N-i}S, M⊗S), sending ξ to multiplication by ξT^{(i)}. In modern terms this is a saturation / 'depth ≥ 2 along the irrelevant ideal' statement for the non-noetherian ring Γ(T), in the spirit of Serre's description of modules on Proj.

Reduction to combinatorics. A degree-i graded S-map f: τ_{N-i}S → M⊗S is determined by f(T^{(k-i)}) = ξ_k T^{(k)} for k ≥ N. S-linearity, comparing f(T^{(ℓ)}T^{(k-i)}) with T^{(ℓ)}f(T^{(k-i)}), gives exactly condition (1) of the previous page: c_{ℓ,k} ξ_k = c_{ℓ,k-i} ξ_{k+ℓ}. Here C_{h,ℓ} = (h+ℓ)!/(h!ℓ!).

The statement proved on this page (k no longer appears) is:
- Theorem. If M is any abelian group and (ξ_k)_{k≥N} satisfies (1), then there is a unique ξ ∈ M with ξ_k = C_{i,k-i} ξ = binom(k,i) ξ for all k ≥ N. This is condition (2).
- Check that (2) solves (1): both sides equal (k+ℓ)!/(ℓ! i! (k-i)!) ξ.

Step 1 of the proof (this page): reduction to the case where M is a Z_(p)-module (localization, not p-adic completion). This assumes two things:
- the theorem holds for Z_(p)-modules;
- for each prime p there is some k ≥ N with p ∤ binom(k,i).
Then the binom(k,i), k ≥ N, have gcd 1, so some finite combination gives Σ m_α binom(k_α,i) = 1.
- Uniqueness: any ξ satisfying (2) must equal Σ m_α ξ_{k_α}.
- Existence: define ξ by that formula. The identity ξ_k = binom(k,i)ξ can be checked after localizing at every prime, because M → ∏_p M_(p) is injective. In M_(p) the local theorem gives some ξ'_p with ξ_k = binom(k,i) ξ'_p. Then ξ = Σ m_α binom(k_α,i) ξ'_p = ξ'_p, which proves the identity.

Step 2 (next page): k = i + p^ε with p^ε > i gives p ∤ binom(k,i), via Lucas. Subtracting the candidate solution reduces the local case to a vanishing corollary: if a solution of (1) vanishes at some h_0 with p ∤ binom(h_0,i), it vanishes identically.
errors: Notational slip: in two places the text writes C_{k,k-i} ('i.e. C_{k,k-i} ∈ Z_p^*', 'Les C_{k,k-i} (k≥N)', and in the final displayed formula). With the stated convention C_{h,ℓ} = (h+ℓ)!/(h!ℓ!), the intended coefficient is C_{i,k-i} = binom(k,i); C_{k,k-i} would be binom(2k-i,k). The argument is correct with C_{i,k-i}.

Minor gap, easily filled: existence in the general case silently uses that the localized family's solution ξ'_p coincides with the image of ξ = Σ m_α ξ_{k_α}. This follows from the Bezout relation, and from injectivity of M → ∏_p M_(p). Neither point is stated, but both are routine.

ideas.what: Graded S-linear maps τ_{N-i}S → M⊗S for S the divided-power polynomial algebra are all given by multiplication by ξT^{(i)}; equivalently M⊗Γ(T) is recovered from its truncations (saturation / Ext vanishing against truncations)
ideas.modern_name: saturation (depth ≥ 2 / vanishing of H^0, H^1 along the irrelevant ideal) of free modules over the divided-power algebra
ideas.usually_credited_to: general framework: Serre (FAC) for graded modules and Proj; the divided-power instance is folklore
ideas.where_published: Analogous statements for polynomial rings appear in EGA II/III (graded modules and Proj); the divided-power version is unsure

ideas.what: Local-to-global reduction for an identity in an abelian group via Bezout on binomial coefficients with gcd 1 and localization at all primes
ideas.modern_name: localization / local-global principle for abelian groups; gcd of binomial coefficients via Lucas' theorem

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but elementary combinatorial lemma (binomial-coefficient functional equations, local-global reduction) serving a saturation statement for the divided-power polynomial algebra. Everything is standard; its only interest is as documentation of how Grothendieck set up the PD de Rham complex in 1976.
transcription_corrections: Heading 'Dém (1)' is 'Dém ①' (circled 1), marking step 1 of the proof rather than referring to equation (1).
In the line 'k = k(p) tel que ... C_{i,k-i} ≢ 0 (p)' there is a struck-out Σ-like symbol before C in the manuscript.
The first display reads '(2) ξ_k = C_{i,k-i} ξ (= binom(k,i) ξ) pour tout k ≥ N', with the index i overwritten on an earlier letter.
